title: The Passage of the Upper Fly River
premise: Ulyana Okafor, estranged from her archaeologist father Dr. Emeka Okafor, learns his expedition up the Fly River has gone silent and that he owes a dangerous debt she has inherited. Joining a salvage crew led by the enigmatic boatman Tevita, she battles the monsoon, a rival treasure syndicate, and her own resentment as the river reveals what her father really found — a site worth killing for. Betrayals surface within the crew, forcing Ulyana to choose between loyalty to her newfound companions and the truth about her father's deception. In the end she saves Tevita and the crew, lets her father face the river's judgment, and burns the map that corrupted everyone who touched it, finding family not in blood but in the boat that carried her home.
about_author: August Okonkwo is the pen name of a former river guide turned novelist who spent a decade working the waterways of Papua New Guinea and West Africa. Their fiction blends hard-edged adventure with intimate questions of inheritance and belonging.

chapters.title: The Debt in the Drawer
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Working docks in Port Moresby, Ulyana receives a lawyer's letter: her father's expedition has gone silent up the Fly River, and a loan shark claims she inherited his debt. She finds his old brass compass mailed to her, its needle spinning wrong. Emotional beat: resentment sharpening into reluctant obligation as she decides to go upriver.

chapters.title: A Boat Called Mercy
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She hires passage with Tevita, a laconic boatman with a leaking boat and a crew of three misfits: engineer Sefina, ex-soldier Bram, and radio operator Junie. Tevita warns her the syndicate man Kessler is also heading upriver. Emotional beat: wary first bonds forming over engine grease and shared suspicion.

chapters.title: Static on the Middle Reach
chapters.summary: Junie's POV. The crew picks up fragments of the expedition's last transmission — a coordinates burst and a scream cut short. They find an abandoned supply camp, looted but recently. Kessler's faster boat shadows them. Emotional beat: dread replacing adventure as Ulyana realizes someone wants the expedition silenced, not rescued.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Tevita's POV. Tevita reveals he owes Ulyana's father a life debt from years ago, complicating his neutrality. A monsoon squall forces the crew to shelter in a limestone cave where Ulyana finds her father's field journal page — evidence he found something he lied about to his funders. Emotional beat: Tevita's guarded loyalty cracking open; Ulyana's image of her father darkening.

chapters.title: The Syndicate's Bargain
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Kessler boards their boat at a fuel stop, offering to forgive the debt in exchange for the compass, which he claims is a key to the site. Ulyana refuses; Bram secretly takes Kessler's card. Emotional beat: the corrupting pull of easy money, and Ulyana's first taste of power over others' fates.

chapters.title: Leaking
chapters.summary: Sefina's POV. The boat takes real damage in rapids; Sefina and Ulyana patch her in waist-deep water through the night while Bram quietly radios Kessler. Junie intercepts the transmission but says nothing yet. Emotional beat: found family solidifying under strain — and the first hairline fracture of betrayal running beneath it.

chapters.title: The Father of All Rivers
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. They find the expedition camp: her father alive, half-mad, guarding a flooded cavern of artifacts while two of his team lie dead — one by accident, one by murder. He confesses he stole the compass from a local custodian family and forged permits. Emotional beat: the reunion she wanted becoming the reckoning she feared; loyalty vs. truth made flesh.

chapters.title: Bram's Price
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Kessler's men raid the camp at dawn. Bram's betrayal is exposed mid-battle; Junie is wounded shielding Ulyana. Bram, horrified by what Kessler intends — killing witnesses and stripping the site — turns his gun on the syndicate instead. Emotional beat: a traitor's redemption purchased at the cost of trust, and the crew's survival hanging by a rope line.

chapters.title: High Water
chapters.summary: Ulyana and Tevita's alternating POV. The monsoon peaks; the river floods the cavern. Ulyana must choose: save the artifacts, save her father, or save Tevita, who is pinned by the capsizing boat. She saves Tevita; her father, clinging to a crate of gold, is swept into the current. Emotional beat: the climax — power, greed, and love weighed in a single drowning moment.

chapters.title: Downstream
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The flood recedes. Ulyana gives the compass to the custodian family's surviving elder, settles her father's debt with Kessler's own evidence, and burns the site map. The crew of the Mercy, now her family, turns downstream together. Emotional beat: quiet resolution — truth chosen over loyalty to the dead, and a new loyalty chosen freely over the living.
